steps.npc: What? You haven't heard of me? The great Mia Persten of the Order of Wizards? The leading researcher in teleportation magic? The creator of the Home Teleport spell?

steps.player: Oh, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to offend you. I'm [player name].

steps.npc: No offence taken! My research tends to take me far from the Wizards' Tower. I've been all across Gielinor and even to some other planes of existence!

steps.player: Other planes of existence? Sounds exciting!

options.text: So what are you doing in Al Kharid?

steps.player: So what are you doing in Al Kharid?

steps.npc: Should I not be in Al Kharid?

steps.player: Er... good question. I guess I just haven't seen a wizard around here before.

steps.npc: Well, maybe you should start expecting the unexpected! That way you can spend less time worrying about why I'm here, and more time asking life's real questions.

steps.player: Right... and what kind of questions are you referring to?

steps.npc: Well, that's the thing. It's different for everyone! Why do trees grow from stumps substantially faster than from seeds? Where do meteorites come from? Why do we have to hold our arms out to teleport successfully?

steps.player: I don't know. What are the answers?
So you're in Al Kharid to work out how trees grow?

steps.npc: No, silly! I came here to buy something.
That's right! Something! Tell me, what do you know of runecrafting?
A shame. Unfortunately, this something requires some understanding in that area.

options.text: What's a wizard doing in Al Kharid?

steps.player: What's a wizard doing in Al Kharid?

steps.npc: Why shouldn't a wizard be in Al Kharid?

steps.player: Er... good question. I guess I just haven't seen a wizard around here before.

steps.npc: Well for a start, I'm not just any wizard. The name's Mia Persten. I'm the leading researcher in teleportation magic for the Order of Wizards.

steps.player: Pleased to meet you. I'm [player name].

steps.npc: Now as for your question, maybe you should start expecting the unexpected! That way you can spend less time worrying about why I'm here, and more time asking life's real questions.
